blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Campbell Valley is a rural sub-area of the Township of Langley in south Langley, not a municipality.
A Campbell Valley label on a property is a board sub-area label, not a statement that the parcel is a farm, is in the ALR, or sits beside the regional park.
The residential stock mixes large acreage lots with occasional small rural lots inside the same sub-area label, so street and parcel checks matter more here than an area boundary.
Zoning varies property to property across the whole Township under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are estate and acreage houses: detached homes on large rural lots, with barns and outbuildings on the equestrian and hobby-farm parcels.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Building more than the permitted number of ALR residences, or a larger residence than the size limits, requires Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) approval.

The Township adopted small-scale multi-unit housing Bylaw 6020 on November 18, 2024: three units on lots of 280 m² or less, four units on lots between 280 m² and 4,050 m², and lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible, so most Campbell Valley acreage parcels fall outside it.
A building permit is required for all secondary suites in the Township, and suites must conform to municipal bylaws and provincial health and safety standards.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Campbell Valley Regional Park's trails are shared by walkers, cyclists and horseback riders, with forests, fields and wetlands and a Nature House, per Metro Vancouver.
The Township separated utility billing from property taxes in 2025, so a Campbell Valley owner now receives a separate annual utility statement for the services that apply.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: development and new projects

items.t: The Township's Bylaw 6020 small-scale multi-unit housing framework, adopted November 18, 2024, is the main recent rule change touching smaller Campbell Valley lots, because lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Township's 2026 flat-rate fees are water $779.96 and sanitary sewer $716.47 for a single-family dwelling, with secondary suite fees of $233.99 for water and $214.94 for sewer.
Garbage in 2026 is a $226.00 base rate plus a cart charge of $200.00 for a 240-litre cart or $100.00 for a 120-litre cart, for properties receiving municipal collection.
Township property taxes and utility fees were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, and utility fees are no longer included on the property tax statement.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Confirm ALR status first, because it caps residences, suite form and subdivision. The ALC states local governments may further restrict ALR residences through zoning, including number, size limits and siting.
Check well and septic records for any rural lot not on Township water and sewer; the Township's utility pages describe serviced properties only and do not certify a specific lot's systems.

blocks.text: What is not confirmed about Campbell Valley Houses

items.t: Parcel-level ALR status, zoning, permitted dwellings and barns, well/septic/water-filtration position, SD35 catchment schools for specific addresses, any TransLink route serving a specific parcel, an area-typical lot size or build era, and property transfer tax / GST apportionment on a specific farm purchase.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley is rural acreage and equestrian country in south Langley, built around Campbell Valley Regional Park and close to the U.S. border.

faq.q: Can an estate lot here carry a second detached dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land, generally no, unless the parcel qualifies for one additional residence. Township zoning may be more restrictive and cannot be more permissive.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a Campbell Valley lot?
faq.a: Subdivision is a two-gate question here, Township and, on ALR land, the ALC. In the ALR, a plan that causes subdivision, including a strata plan, may not be registered without ALC approval or a permitted exception.

faq.q: Does a house here come on sewer and city water?
faq.a: Do not assume it, because rural lots can be on well and septic. The Township's utility statements cover properties that receive water, sanitary sewer and garbage services, and owners receive a statement only for the services that apply to their property. Ask which services the specific lot actually has, and price well and septic checks into due diligence.

faq.q: What does a secondary suite cost each year here?
faq.a: A suite adds a set percentage to Township utility fees, on top of the permit. Secondary suite water and sewer fees are 30% of the annual flat-rate fees, and from 2025 properties with suites are also subject to an Annual Secondary Suite Infrastructure Fee collected with property taxes. A permit is required before the suite is built.
